shortDescription: The Baltic Exchange's dry bulk freight index, which tracks rates for ships carrying dry bulk commodities, rose on Wednesday, buoyed by stronger rates across all categories.

children: The Baltic Exchange's dry bulk freight index, which tracks rates for ships carrying dry bulk commodities, rose on Wednesday, buoyed by stronger rates across all categories.
, which tracks rates for capesize, panamax and supramax vessels, rose 36 points, or 1%, to 3,620.
The capesize index (.BACI) was up 87 points, or 1.4%, at 6,400.
Average daily earnings for capesize vessels (.BATCA), which typically transport 150,000-ton cargoes, including iron ore and coal, increased by $788 to $54,538.

However, iron ore prices fell after a four-session winning streak, weighed down by concerns over demand in top consumer China as steelmakers cut output amid shrinking margins, while higher ore imports also added pressure.
The panamax index (.BPNI) was unchanged at 2,414.
Average daily earnings for panamax vessels (.BPWT), which usually carry 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, rose $1 to $21,725.
The supramax index (.BSIS) was up 11 points, or 0.7%, at 1,704.
